primary_diagnosis_treated: Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease – Stage 5 (CKD‑5) with hypertension, proteinuria, ischemic heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and anemia
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg PO once daily, titrate by 1.25 mg every 2 weeks to target 5 mg PO daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression; control blood pressure
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & K⁺ after 1‑2 weeks

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily, titrate up to 80 mg BID based on volume status, weight, and edema
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any dose change
medications.purpose: Volume control in CKD‑5 (eGFR < 30 mL/min) where thiazides are ineffective
medications.nice_justification: CKD management recommends diuretics for hypertension/volume overload; loop diuretic preferred when eGFR < 30 (NG203)

medications.dose: 20 mg PO once daily (increase to 40 mg if LDL‑C target not met after 6 weeks)
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: All CKD patients should receive a statin for CVD risk reduction

medications.dose: 10 units SC once daily, titrate by 2‑4 U every 3‑4 days to fasting glucose 4‑7 mmol/L
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control; metformin contraindicated at eGFR < 30
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management in CKD recommends insulin when eGFR < 30 (NICE NG28/NG179 guidance)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg PO once daily, titrate to 5‑10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review heart rate and BP every 3 months
medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of ischemic heart disease and additional BP lowering
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 (IHD) recommends beta‑blocker for stable angina; compatible with CKD

medications.dose: 25 000 IU SC/IV weekly, dose-adjusted to maintain Hb 10‑12 g/dL
medications.duration: Until Hb target achieved, then review quarterly
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of CKD (Hb < 10 g/dL) after iron repletion
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 anemia section: ESA when Hb < 10 g/dL and iron stores repleted

interactions_checked.interaction: ACE‑I may raise serum potassium while HCTZ lowers potassium; net effect unpredictable and risk of hyper‑ or hypokalaemia.
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum K⁺ 1‑2 weeks after starting Ramipril; consider discontinuing HCTZ when furosemide is initiated.

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive diuretic effect → risk of volume depletion, hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia.
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue Hydrochlorothiazide once furosemide is started; monitor electrolytes, weight, BP.

interactions_checked.interaction: Hypokalaemia from diuretics can impair insulin sensitivity and increase hypoglycaemia risk.
interactions_checked.action: Check potassium and glucose; adjust insulin dose if needed.

contraindications.reason: eGFR 4 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – high risk of lactic acidosis.
CKD‑5; NSAIDs accelerate progression and cause fluid retention.
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for analgesia; avoid OTC NSAIDs.

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; guideline prohibits dual RAAS blockade.

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, creatinine trend, and bicarbonate not provided – will be measured before initiating ACE‑I and loop diuretic.
Liver function tests not available – required before starting atorvastatin.
HbA1c, fasting glucose, and detailed diabetes regimen not supplied – insulin dose will be titrated to target glucose.
Hemoglobin, ferritin, TSAT not provided – ESA initiation assumes iron repletion has been confirmed.
Allergy status unknown – will verify no ACE‑I, statin, or insulin allergy before prescribing.
treatment_summary: The plan introduces an ACE inhibitor (Ramipril) and loop diuretic (Furosemide) to control hypertension and volume overload, replaces the ineffective thiazide, adds a statin (Atorvastatin) for CVD risk reduction, initiates basal insulin for diabetes (metformin contraindicated), adds a beta‑blocker (Bisoprolol) for stable angina, and provides ESA therapy for CKD‑related anemia. All choices follow NICE NG203 recommendations, consider the patient’s eGFR = 4 mL/min, and include monitoring and safety actions.
